hawaii.enforce_note: Non-competes are not banned for all workers, but they are void for employees of a technology business, while other workers are judged under the state's general restraint-of-trade law.
hawaii.state_note: A non-compete or non-solicit clause in a technology-business employee's contract is void and of no force and effect, while sale-of-business and trade-secret covenants remain lawful under the same statute.
hawaii.statute_name: Hawaii Revised Statutes § 480-4 (Combinations in restraint of trade prohibited)
hawaii.threshold_note: There is no earnings threshold; the ban turns on working for a technology business, not on how much the worker earns.

idaho.enforce_note: Non-competes are enforceable for a key employee or key independent contractor if the restriction is reasonable in duration, geography, and type of work and no broader than needed to protect a legitimate business interest.
idaho.state_note: A non-compete of 18 months or less is presumed reasonable as to duration, and a court may modify an overbroad covenant to make it reasonable rather than striking it entirely.
idaho.statute_name: Idaho Code, Title 44, Chapter 27 — Agreements and Covenants Protecting Legitimate Business Interests
idaho.threshold_note: There is no earnings threshold; the statute applies only to key employees, and an employee is presumed key if paid in the top 5% of the employer's workforce.

illinois.enforce_note: Non-competes are void unless the employee's actual or expected annualized earnings exceed the statutory threshold, and they must also pass notice, consideration, and reasonableness requirements.
illinois.state_note: The employer must give the worker a copy of the agreement at least 14 calendar days before employment starts and advise the worker in writing to consult an attorney.
illinois.threshold_note: A non-compete is void if the employee earns $75,000 per year or less in 2026, and the threshold rises to $80,000 on January 1, 2027, then $85,000 in 2032 and $90,000 in 2037.

indiana.enforce_note: Non-competes are generally enforceable for most workers if reasonable in scope, duration, and geography, with the rules coming from court decisions rather than a general statute.
indiana.state_note: Physicians are treated differently: non-competes with primary care physicians are banned, and non-competes between physicians and hospitals are void for agreements entered on or after July 1, 2025.
indiana.threshold_note: There is no earnings threshold; enforceability turns on reasonableness, not on pay.

iowa.enforce_note: Non-competes are generally enforceable if they pass the Iowa Supreme Court's three-part test: reasonably necessary to protect the employer's business, not unreasonably restrictive of the worker, and not harmful to the public interest.
iowa.state_note: An Iowa court may narrow an overbroad clause and enforce the trimmed version instead of voiding it, and licensed mental health professionals cannot be bound by a non-compete at all.
iowa.threshold_note: There is no earnings threshold; pay does not decide enforceability in Iowa.

kansas.enforce_note: Non-competes are enforceable if the restraint is reasonable under the circumstances, protects a legitimate business interest, and is not harmful to the public welfare.
kansas.state_note: Kansas courts construe non-competes strictly against the employer, and a clause whose only purpose is to avoid ordinary competition is unenforceable.
kansas.threshold_note: There is no earnings threshold; enforceability turns on reasonableness, not on pay.

kentucky.enforce_note: Non-competes are generally enforceable if they protect a legitimate business interest and are reasonable in time, geography, and scope, with the rules coming from court decisions rather than a statute.
kentucky.state_note: An existing at-will employee must receive something new, such as a raise, promotion, or specialized training, for signing a non-compete — continued employment alone is not enough consideration.
kentucky.threshold_note: There is no earnings threshold; enforceability turns on reasonableness and consideration, not on pay.

louisiana.enforce_note: Non-competes are null and void by default and enforceable only if they fit a narrow statutory exception for employees, business sellers, partners, or shareholders.
louisiana.state_note: An employee non-compete must name the specific parishes or municipalities where competition is barred, where the employer carries on a like business, and it may last no more than two years after employment ends.
louisiana.statute_name: Louisiana Revised Statutes § 23:921 (Restraint of business prohibited)
louisiana.threshold_note: There is no earnings threshold; enforceability turns on meeting the statute's strict time and geography requirements, not on pay.

maine.enforce_note: Non-competes are contrary to public policy and enforceable only if reasonable and no broader than necessary to protect trade secrets, confidential information, or goodwill.
maine.state_note: The employer must disclose before the job offer that a non-compete will be required and give the worker a copy at least 3 business days before signing, and a violation can draw a civil fine of at least $5,000.
maine.threshold_note: An employer may not require a non-compete from a worker earning at or below 400% of the federal poverty level, a figure that rises with household size and is adjusted annually.
maine.wage_threshold: 400% of the federal poverty level (about $63,840 for one person in 2026)

maryland.enforce_note: Non-competes are generally enforceable above the statutory wage floor if reasonable in duration, geography, and scope, but they are void for lower-paid workers.
maryland.state_note: Non-competes are also void for most licensed health-care workers who provide direct patient care and earn $350,000 or less, and for all veterinary practitioners and technicians.
maryland.statute_name: Maryland Code, Labor and Employment § 3-716 (Noncompete or conflict of interest provision in contract)
maryland.threshold_note: A non-compete is void for an employee earning at or below 150% of the state minimum wage, which is $22.50 per hour or about $46,800 per year at the $15.00 state minimum wage in 2026, so the floor rises if the minimum wage rises.
